scalars.scalar_value: RECRUITMENT PERIOD ONE MONTH: Applicants will be screened after two weeks; and then on a weekly basis.  The position can be filled prior to the apply by date.
Experience with assisted reproductive technology of livestock, field medicine and triage, including but not limited to anesthesia, castration, IV fluid administration, venipuncture.

Experience with livestock anatomy, behavior and basic physiology, husbandry, handling, moving, restraining livestock (cattle, sheep, pigs or goats) including fractious and aggressive livestock, must be able to identify and describe abnormal physical signs and appearances.
Hours to be arranged. Will include early mornings and some late nights. Occasional weekends and holidays.

items.item_text: Must possess a Veterinary Assistant Controlled Substance Permit (VACSP) or obtain within 3 months of date of hire.
Required to hold a valid California driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program

Experience with livestock anatomy, behavior and basic physiology, husbandry, handling, moving, restraining livestock (cattle, sheep, pigs or goats) including fractious and aggressive livestock, must be able to identify and describe abnormal physical signs and appearances.
Experience with assisted reproductive technology of livestock, field medicine and triage, including but not limited to anesthesia, castration, IV fluid administration, venipuncture.
Experience administering vaccines, medication PO, IV, SQ & IM.
Experience with euthanasia of livestock including utilization of a captive bolt.
Experience using computer programs including; Microsoft Applications (Word, Excel, Outlook).
Experience working with populations/herds of animals and have basic understanding herd health concepts.

Under general supervision, provides technical and clinical support for the Livestock Herd Health and Reproduction Service within the Veterinary Medical Teaching Hospital (VMTH). The position supports herd health and reproductive management programs through coordination of clinical operations, maintenance of medical and reproductive records, implementation of established protocols, and technical assistance with specialized reproductive services. This role contributes to high-quality patient care, client service, teaching, and research while promoting animal welfare, biosecurity, and operational efficiency in both hospital and field settings.

Excellent interpersonal and problem-solving skills with the skills to effectively communicate with a diverse group of clients, faculty, residents and students, verbally and in writing with excellent penmanship and the skills to transcribe numbers without confusion.
Knowledge of medications commonly used in livestock.
Good organizational skills to prioritize daily/weekly workload with skills to recognize and handle difficult/unpleasant situations and/or individuals.
Knowledge of infection control programs, dairy records systems, livestock reproduction programs and basis preventive medicine herd health programs.
